I got a ticket for fishing without a license in Oregon. I understand I fucked up but didn't quite realize the severity until I noticed the $475.00 fine. I plan on pleading either guilty or no contest but am curious which decision may persuade for greater leniency from the judge.

Should I plead Guilty or No Contest for greater leniency from a judge?
Plead guilty and do some community service with the park service between now and court.

This kind of question is highly specific not just to local practices, but to the judge hearing the case.

That said, in my long-ago, limited experience with judges from another state, it generally makes no difference for a crime like this. In all likelihood, the judge is not going to split hairs over whether you plead "no contest" or "guilty" to this kind of charge. More important will be communicating that you are taking responsibility for your action and that it won't happen again.

As another poster said, talk tot he prosecutor ahead of time. Depending on local practice, your criminal record and the whim of the prosecutor, you may even be eligible for some kind of diversion or deferred adjudication program that might result in the charges being dismissed entirely.

6 months ago I had a good reason to start hanging out on /trees (on some other website you probably never heard of) and also hanging out on a few online radio stations.

Some of the classic rock stations also have a good mix of some current rock as well, and I am hearing a lot of groups for the first time that I really enjoy, and would like to know what 'signature' albums I should look into to get the best introduction.

For an example to make sure I'm asking correctly, these were a few of the albums that I consider to be a group's 'defining' work - not necessarily their best-selling or most popular, but the one where everything just seemed to coalesce (and in some cases, was actually a departure from any of their previous work) - and I'd like to know if any more recent groups / artists have captured that magic:

Fleetwood Mac - Rumours (The group was going through some personality conflicts, and were far from their original blues-driven beginning [sans women] but knocked it out of the park with their tight harmonies, excellent production, and very on-task performances.)

Styx - Grand Illusion (Still sounding like a rock band, not yet a ballad-generating pop band. Great guitar and bass work, spot-on keyboards, and great lyrical journeys.)

Supertramp - Breakfast in America (At the time, some of these songs were so well-recorded and performed that I was skeptical that vinyl would ever give way to digital!)

Genesis - Selling England by the Pound (and Wind and Wuthering - those 2 should have been a double album.)

Yes - Fragile (OK, maybe 90125 as well)

Jackson Browne - Running on Empty

Pink Floyd - Dark Side (I know... but I like all of their stuff, believe me!)

edit

I appreciate all of the feedback - Can't wait to get home and check some of these out!

New Stuff:

Micachu and the Shapes - Never [Pop / Experimental] -- Calling it a pop album is a bit of a stretch by today's standards. But as someone who judges all pop albums by comparing it to the Beatles' Revolver, I'm going to say that it is one of the best pop albums ever made. It may take some time to get used to the electronics and lo-fi aesthetics. Give it a chance and it's very rewarding.

Ought - More Than Any Other Day [Art Punk] -- Their only album released so far, but it's an incredibly coherent statement. I especially enjoy the optimistic lyrics, and the instrumentals are great.

2000's:

The Mars Volta - Frances the Mute [Prog Rock] -- The 2000's saw a reawakening of progressive rock. Prog rockers of the day were quick to incorporate post-hardcore into their music. The Mars Volta was arguably the best prog rock group of the decade. Their combination of post-hardcore, Led Zeppelin styled blues rock, latin jazz, and avant garde experimentation is truly unique and quite engaging.

Coheed & Cambria - Apollo, I'm Burning Star IV, Vol. I: From Fear Through the Eyes of Madness [Prog Rock] -- Great guitars, and a wonderful mix of metal, pop, and post-hardcore.

Portugal. The Man - The Satanic Satanist [Indie Rock] -- Some danceable, party rock from a band with a period in the middle of their name.

Animal Collective - Sung Tongs [Neo-Psychedelia] -- It's a bit of a stretch to say that this is their defining album, as all their albums are completely different. Anyway, it's some of the greatest trippy music I've ever heard.

1990's:

Modest Mouse - Lonesome Crowded West [Indie Rock] -- Some of the most profound lyrics ever written over the top of punk- and folk-inspired indie rock tunes.

Neutral Milk Hotel - In the Aeroplane over the Sea [Indie Rock] -- An album about a boy that falls in love with Ann Frank. Some incredibly dark moments and twisted lyricism on this one.
